title: Flat, the folder tower, the city and the street
description: Which of its ways in the page shows, and how the reader moves between them: Flat, Cyberspace's folder tower, its city and the city's street, and the flat view a ~space address gets where Cyberspace can't run. The address decides it: route() reads its last segment, and every move here either changes the address (a new history entry, so Back and Forward retrace it) or replaces the entry (a selection, a floor slid back, walking). The skyline (step 6 of the plan) is not built yet.

states.description: The flat page: the folder column, and the folder's drawings, cards and tables. The address has no ~space segment.

Cyberspace's folder tower: the address folder as a stack of glass floors, one per .dev file, drawn at the bottom, then written, then knowledge, with labels and group brackets on the left, the folder's card and the pulled-out floor's card on the right. One drawn floor at a time is pulled out to the right with its city standing on it, small; the address names it (#<folder>|view:<file>|~space), or names none (#<folder>|~space, the first drawn view). A written or knowledge floor's inspector can be open in place of the cards. The status line says how many floors the tower has; its hint, Scroll to climb · click a floor to pull it out.

Cyberspace's city: one drawn view (#<folder>|view:<file>|~space:city, or a part's focus with it selected) standing full size on the ground, with its labels, legend and camera controls; a selected part lights its beams and opens the inspector. The status line's hint is Esc goes up a level.

Cyberspace's street: the city's own meshes seen from eye height (#<folder>|<kind>:<part>|~space:street, walked to that part, or #<folder>|view:<file>|~space:street, to the middle of the city), 61.2° of view with its centre low, a vignette and a crosshair. The reader walks with W A S D or the arrows, looks by dragging, rises and sinks with Space and Z; towers are solid and plates are steps. The breadcrumb, the key hints, the map and, over a part under the pointer, the hover card take the place of the city's legend and camera controls. The status line says where the eye walks; its hint, Esc rises back to orbit.

A ~space address where Cyberspace can't run: the flat view of the place before the marker, with the status line saying Cyberspace needs WebGL, which this browser has turned off. Showing the flat view. The Flat / Cyberspace switch is hidden.

transitions.trigger: the address gains ~space or ~space:tower (a link, or the switch once it shows)
transitions.guard: the browser has WebGL 2 and three.js loads
transitions.action: three.js is imported on the first entry; the tower stands at once, the view the address names (or the folder's first drawn view) pulled out, the camera in its opening pose

transitions.trigger: the address gains ~space:city
transitions.guard: the browser has WebGL 2 and three.js loads
transitions.action: the city of the view or part it names stands, fitted to the room the panels leave

transitions.trigger: the address gains ~space
transitions.guard: no WebGL 2 context can be had, or a WebGLRenderer can't be made

transitions.trigger: the address gains ~space
transitions.action: the status line says Cyberspace couldn't load its 3D library. Showing the flat view; the next entry tries again

transitions.trigger: a click on a drawn floor that is not out
transitions.action: a new history entry #<folder>|view:<file>|~space; the floor out slides back as this one slides out with its city, 450 ms eased out, at once with reduced motion

transitions.trigger: Slide back, or Esc with no inspector open
transitions.action: the floor slides back and the entry is replaced with #<folder>|~space; until the reader goes elsewhere every floor stays in. With none out Esc does nothing yet

transitions.trigger: a click on a written or knowledge floor, or an address naming one (view:<file>, entity:<file>[#<record id>])
transitions.action: the inspector opens on that floor (title, kind, description, the record named, Read it in Flat) in place of the cards, its edges in --hot, and the entry is replaced with its address; Esc or a click on empty ground closes it and the entry is the tower's again

transitions.trigger: Enter the city, a double-click on the pulled-out floor, or Enter
transitions.guard: the models can't build the view on it
transitions.action: the inspector opens on that floor with why, and Read it in Flat

transitions.trigger: a folder's chip under Inside on the folder card
transitions.action: a new history entry #<folder>|~space; that folder's tower stands at once

transitions.trigger: Enter the city, a double-click on the pulled-out floor, or Enter
transitions.guard: the view on it was built
transitions.action: a new history entry #<folder>|view:<file>|~space:city; the camera flies to the floor until its city fills the room the city's panels leave (600 ms), then in one frame the full-size city takes the small one's place, seen as it was, and the tower fades out behind it (200 ms). At once with reduced motion; input on the way lands it where the eye is

transitions.trigger: Esc with nothing selected
transitions.action: a new history entry #<folder>|view:<file>|~space; in one frame the tower stands with this city pulled out on its floor, seen as the city was, fading in over 200 ms, and the camera flies to the tower's opening pose (600 ms). At once with reduced motion

transitions.trigger: Back or Forward to the tower address of the city's own view
transitions.action: as Esc does; to a tower address with another view out, the tower stands at once

transitions.trigger: Back or Forward to a city address of the tower's folder
transitions.action: as Enter the city does, the view it names pulled out first if it isn't

transitions.trigger: Enter its folder on a selected part that has views of its own, or a link in the inspector to a view or record
transitions.action: a new history entry; that folder's tower stands at once, with the view pulled out or the floor's inspector open

transitions.trigger: a click on a tower, plate or beacon; Esc or a click on empty ground with one selected
transitions.action: the part is selected or cleared, and the entry is replaced with its address or the view's own

transitions.trigger: Walk to <name> in the inspector, or Walk in the camera controls
transitions.action: a new history entry #<folder>|<kind>:<part>|~space:street (#<folder>|view:<file>|~space:street with nothing selected); the camera flies from the orbit pose to the street's, 12 units from the part across the layout's flow, eased on an arc for 400 ms and 12 more a unit travelled (500 to 1200), and the HUD changes when it lands. At once with reduced motion; input on the way lands it where the eye is

transitions.trigger: the address gains ~space:street
transitions.guard: the browser has WebGL 2 and three.js loads
transitions.action: the city of the view or part it names stands, and the eye is put in the street at once

transitions.trigger: Back or Forward to a street address
transitions.action: the city stands at once, and the eye is put in the street, where the reader walked in that entry if they did

transitions.trigger: W A S D or the arrows, Alt with ← →, a drag, Space or Z
transitions.action: the eye walks at 6 units a second (14 with Shift), turns, looks (pitch within ±60°), rises or sinks (1.7 to 30 above the ground), sliding along towers and stepping onto plates over 150 ms; the history entry is replaced, its state holding where the eye is, at most four times a second

transitions.trigger: a click on a part, Enter on the part under the crosshair, or Esc with one selected
transitions.action: the part is selected or cleared and the entry replaced, as in the city; the eye stays

transitions.trigger: a click on the map, or Walk to <name> in the inspector
transitions.action: the eye flies there, as high above the ground as it walks, out of any tower; at once with reduced motion

transitions.trigger: Esc with nothing selected, or the breadcrumb's view
transitions.action: a new history entry #<folder>|view:<file>|~space:city; the camera flies back to the orbit pose the reader left, or to the fit where they hadn't moved it or came in by the street, and the city's HUD returns at once. At once with reduced motion

transitions.trigger: Back or Forward to a city address of the street's view
transitions.action: as Esc does

transitions.trigger: Back or Forward to a street address of the city's view
transitions.action: as Walk to does, to where the reader walked in that entry if they did

transitions.trigger: the breadcrumb's folder, or Back or Forward to a tower address of its folder
transitions.action: a new history entry #<folder>|~space for the breadcrumb; the tower stands with this city pulled out, as it does from the city

transitions.trigger: an address without ~space: Open flat, the switch, Back
an address without ~space: Read it in Flat, the switch, Back
an address without ~space: Open flat, the switch, Back
